title: Follow-ups: Frontend Dashboard page (PR #67)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #67 (frontend-dashboard-page), tracked so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: RiskSummaryCard's 6%-rule-breach banner (Box + WarningAmberIcon + Typography with theme.palette.riskBreach styling) is copy-pasted near-verbatim from RiskPanel.tsx's identical banner — only the warning message text differs. Per Frontend.md's Structure Rules (near-duplicates should be consolidated into one shared component instead of copy-pasted across features), consider extracting a shared `RiskBreachBanner` (message as a prop) used by both RiskPanel and RiskSummaryCard.

DashboardPage.tsx defines its own local `formatCurrency` (`toLocaleString(..., {style:'currency',currency:'USD',...})`), identical to PortfolioPage.tsx's own copy — a fourth distinct currency-formatting implementation in the codebase alongside RiskPanel's and PositionsTable's differently-shaped versions (the latter two already flagged in frontend-portfolio-risk-panel-followups). Extract one shared currency formatter so a future formatting change doesn't need updating in four places.

PositionsGlanceTable's `formatNullableCurrency` duplicates the null-check logic already in PositionsTable.tsx's identically-named helper (PositionsTable composes its own local `formatCurrency`, while PositionsGlanceTable inlines the `$${value.toFixed(2)}` string directly) — two independent implementations of 'render a nullable price' that can silently drift apart. Worth consolidating alongside the formatCurrency extraction above.

TickerSearchBox's placement under features/stocks/components/ (rather than components/common/) is a genuinely arguable call: it hardcodes navigation to `/stocks/:ticker` and uppercases input assuming a stock-ticker convention, which is defensible as stock-domain knowledge per Frontend.md §3's literal rule, but the underlying 'text field + submit button that navigates somewhere on submit' pattern is otherwise generic UI behavior. Worth reconsidering if a second lookup-and-navigate entry point appears elsewhere in the app (e.g. when frontend-stock-analysis-page or a future AppShell search bar reuses/duplicates this pattern) — e.g. a common/ `NavigatingSearchBox` taking a route-builder + input-normalizer prop, with the ticker-specific behavior supplied by the caller.
